Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Filing-index table
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from real SEC quarterly and daily index files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table queryable by later stages; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table holds rows parsed from real quarterly and real daily index files, with a row count per source file, fetched with an identifying User-Agent below the SEC's published request ceiling; the findings file records files fetched, bytes, request count and wall time of the real run
      Leaves out: provenance manifest, raw-snapshot replay, versioned publication and golden-fixture validation suite → Stage 4; quarterly reconciliation and daily catch-up → Stage 5; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that filing-index rows name, for a bounded range of real index rows.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: submissions on disk, each traceable to its index row; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: every index row in the chosen range has its submission on disk or a recorded failure; the findings file records files, bytes, request rate, wall time and the extrapolated full-history download time
      Leaves out: resumable full-history download and shared request budget → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk and their index-row links
      Produces: extracted 10-K and 8-K main documents linked to their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: for the Stage 2 range, every 10-K and 8-K row (amendments included) has an extracted main document or a recorded reason it has none; the findings file records counts, failures and extraction time
      Leaves out: extraction over the full history → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Index provenance and replay
      Objective: Make the filing-index table traceable to retained source bytes and rebuildable without re-downloading.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table and findings
      Produces: provenance manifest, raw-snapshot replay, versioned publication and golden-fixture validation suite for the index
      Exit: each table row names its source file and hash; a rebuild from retained raw snapshots with SEC access disabled yields the same rows; the golden-fixture validation suite covers the index formats in the supported range
      Leaves out: quarterly reconciliation and daily catch-up → Stage 5; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Index reconciliation and catch-up
      Objective: Keep the filing-index table current and correct as daily files arrive and quarterly files change.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's provenance manifest and versioned publication
      Produces: quarterly reconciliation and daily catch-up for the index
      Exit: a re-read of changed quarterly files records additions, field changes and withdrawals without losing source history; a run after missed days ingests every unprocessed daily file across quarter boundaries
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full-history submissions
      Objective: Download and handle submissions over the full history as an interruptible campaign.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's download, Stage 3's handling, Stage 5's current index; Stage 2 findings for the time estimate
      Produces: resumable full-history download, shared request budget, extraction over the full history
      Exit: an interrupted run resumes without re-fetching completed submissions; index, submission and extraction runs share one request budget under the SEC ceiling; coverage and gaps are reported per quarter
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run index ingestion, reconciliation and submission handling on a schedule in a chosen deployment.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–6
      Produces: scheduling and deployment, with monitoring and runbooks
      Exit: scheduled runs execute unattended in the deployed environment and their reports show outcomes and gaps; the deployment platform choice is recorded (the Azure ADR is a background option)
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
